description:
See the individual commit messages for more details, but here's an overview:
- Add `consoleTextColor` and `consoleBackgroundColor` values to `UTMConfigurable`, and implement the setters/getters in `UTMConfiguration+Display` that use a keyed archiver to convert the `NSColor` into `NSData` that can be stored in `config.plist`. (This is needed because if I just save the hex values, there is a lot of drift in the color picker because of the loss in converting to/from a hex string, and it's done on each color value change)
- Add `ColorPicker`s to the display console configuration.
- Add and call a Javascript method that sets the color values in the hterm prefs.
- Save the color settings as hex strings when using the apple virtualization backend. This is fine because the conversion is only done on load/save and not on every color change.
- Set the `consoleFontSize` to 12 by default if it's `nil` when using the apple backend.
- Change the `supportedConsoleFonts` method to list all the fonts in each family, to allow maximal customization.
- Implement `supportedConsoleFonts` for macOS (instead of just returning an empty array) to allow picking custom fonts.
- Set the font used in SwiftTerm based on the configuration for the apple backend.

<hr>

@osy Do you think I should squash the [`fix build on iOS`](https://github.com/utmapp/UTM/commit/111576cd781e3fe454d5f7e41de48260197b58a0) commit with the [first commit](https://github.com/utmapp/UTM/commit/18d9be4d702c89cb961fbe529f69428dee2d0078)? They're similar enough and the first one isn't really a 'working' commit because it can't build on iOS.

Also please take a look at the two `TODO`s (I'll post a comment on them since I want to ask a question about them), and remind me to remove them before you merge this.

<hr>

BTW, during my testing, more in the early stages of implementing this, I found that the VMs got reordered in the list, but I'm not sure if it might have been because it's debug builds etc. In the later parts of developing this PR I haven't found this problem any more, so I don't think it's an issue.

comments.body:
I was thinking maybe using a `CGColor` might be a good idea for two reasons:
- SwiftUI's `ColorPicker` can take a binding to a `CGColor`
- It would be compatible with both platforms, the `PlatformColor` stuff wouldn't be needed

But the problem is that `CGColor` isn't an object, so passing it around is harder. And also I'm not sure if `CGColor` can be used with a keyed archiver to save it.

I think it wouldn't be worth the extra trouble, since it isn't that much code in the `Binding` that converts a `NSColor` to the SwiftUI `Color` type.
I don't think using a default value would be necessary here, since default colors are set when migrating the configuration, and also in the `Binding` in the configuration view.

> But the problem is that CGColor isn't an object, so passing it around is harder.

Why is it any harder than say NSInteger?
@osy How would it be done? (What should the property attributes be and do I use `struct CGColor *` or `CGColorRef *`)?
Look at my latest comment, I think NSNumber or NSString would be better fit here.

@osy The alternative solution would be to store an NSColor somewhere in UTMConfiguration, and then convert it to a hex string when saving the plist, like how it's done for the Apple backend.

If you want to do that, how/where should the intermediate NSColor be stored, and where can I put the conversion code?

I think it should be NSString in UTMConfigurable and both QEMU and Apple backends store the hex string.

Then when it's used for QEMU terminal, it uses the hex string directly. For Swift terminal it converts the hex string to NSColor (through your extension) in the view controller when it's being set.
@osy How do we prevent the drift then?

Storage call .hexString

Usage call NSColor(fromHexString: String) which you implemented in the extension but you need to change the init there to call init(srgbRed:green:blue:alpha)

@osy You see, I can do that for the Apple backend because it's only converted when storing, do drift isn't a problem when selecting the color.

It's different with the Qemu backend because when setting or getting the console colors, it will have to do the conversion to save it into the dictionary. And because it's directly bound to the value used in the SwiftUI color picker, a small amount of drift on each conversion will be amplified to the point of not being usable.
Can you try this different multiplier https://stackoverflow.com/a/39358741 seems like UIColor uses extended sRGB

@osy Nope, there's still a (slightly smaller but still noticeable/unusable) amount of drift.

I think the only solution if you want to store the console colors as a hex string is to only do the conversion when saving/loading the plist, not in the setter/getter for the color properties.
Any chance you can ask stackoverflow with details on what you're seeing? I don't think there should be drift and maybe it's a bug that others have workarounds for.
